items.notes: Printed crop holds only bass clef, a sharp, 3/4 and one rest glyph; no noteheads. Source is a 3-note hollow chord with ledger lines then a single stemmed note. All three proposals sit left of the staff.

Source totals fourteen noteheads over thirteen onsets including a 3-note chord, two 2-note chords and three rests. Printed shows a comparable total head count with a rest in the middle and a stacked hollow group near the end, but nine proposals against thirteen onsets is too few to pair anything reliably.

Both panels are extremely sparse with two hollow noteheads and nothing else before the final barline. Source spaces its two onsets apart; the printed stacks its two heads at one horizontal position, so it is unclear whether that is one chord or two events.

Crop is truncated vertically and horizontally: clef, four flats, common time, a tempo word, an internal barline and two clipped noteheads. Source is four evenly spaced quarters; too little is visible to compare.

Printed shows a short low-clef staff fragment cut off at the bottom edge with two barlines and about six single noteheads, while the source needs eleven noteheads over six onsets including a 3-note chord. Truncation makes both count and cardinality unreadable.
Same source shape as R025 (3-note chord, single, 2-note, single, 2-note, 2-note). Printed fragment is again clipped at the bottom and shows only four or five visible heads between two barlines.
Printed crop ends just after the meter, showing only clipped accent marks. Source is a hollow note followed by triplet-bracketed notes; nothing printed is available to compare.
Printed crop is bass clef, sharps and 3/4 only. Source is rest, single note, 3-note chord, rest.

Both panels open with a beamed pair, then a single note, then another beamed pair. Printed carries more heads than the source's seven and runs past the right crop edge, so the closing 2-note chord cannot be checked.

Printed shows a rest before an internal barline and about five detached notes after it, whereas the source has a rest plus three notes. Whether the crop is exactly one measure is unclear, so no structural verdict.
Printed crop holds only treble clef, 2/4 and a clipped mark. Source is two 16th pairs, a flagged note and a rest.
Printed crop is bass clef and 2/4 only, ending before any note content. Source is rest, single note, 2-note chord.

Source is a single 2-note chord followed by a rest and then nothing to the barline. Printed shows a five-note multi-beamed group under long straight and curved marks - a fast run, not a chord-plus-rest measure.

Both panels open with one stacked 2-note chord, matching cardinality. The printed then shows a further single stemmed note where the source has a rest, which is an event-level difference only; the sparse two-onset shape still corresponds.

Source is a 2-note chord then two rests. Printed runs note, dotted dyad, dotted dyad, then a fermata-marked dotted hollow note before the final barline - four sounding onsets where the source has one.

Same source shape as R035 (2-note chord then two rests) but the printed crop spans a clef change and carries a dotted chord, two more notes and a fermata-marked hollow note - far more sounding content than the source.

Both panels are two stacked 2-note chord events and nothing else. Printed ties the second hollow chord to the first, where the source has a rest at that onset; the single printed chord pairs cleanly with X1 on cardinality.

No proposals at all. Printed shows one hollow notehead below the staff under a tie arc and otherwise an empty staff to the final barline; source is one note then a rest, so the shape agrees and the printed carries no rest.

Single-onset measure. Printed adds a low filled note ahead of a wavy arpeggio line and a fermata-marked hollow chord of about three noteheads; the source onset is a 2-note chord, so cardinality disagrees while the one-chord shape corresponds.

Single-onset measure: source is one stacked hollow chord with ledger lines. Printed shows a wavy arpeggio spanning the staff with hollow noteheads inside it before the final barline. Head count inside the roll cannot be resolved, so cardinality is left open.
